desktop_mission.voice_mission: Today we're simulating the Stirling heat engine, the regenerative thermal cycle, and the Schmidt analysis in Kotlin.
math_cards: W_net = ∮ P dV = n · R · (T_H - T_C) · ln(r_v)
Net mechanical shaft work equals the enclosed area of the closed P-V indicator loop
Ideal thermodynamic efficiency matches the theoretical maximum reversible Carnot ceiling
P(θ) = n · R / Σ [ V_i(θ) / T_i ]
Instantaneous gas pressure arises from continuous 90° phase-shifted volume variation
desktop_mission.voice_math: The core physics: closed-cycle indicated work, the Carnot efficiency limit, and Schmidt pressure kinematics.

math_steps.note: Harmonic piston volume variations govern instantaneous cycle pressure
math_steps.code:
// 1. Schmidt equation for closed engine pressure
val tRegenLogMean = max(1f, (hotTempK - coldTempK) / max(0.01f, ln(hotTempK / max(coldTempK, 1f))))
val effectiveTRegen = coldTempK + (tRegenLogMean - coldTempK) * regeneratorEff
val denom = (vHotCm3 / max(hotTempK, 1f)) + (vColdCm3 / max(coldTempK, 1f)) + (deadVolCm3 / max(effectiveTRegen, 1f))
val pressureKPa = max(40f, (gasConstantMolesNR / max(denom, 0.001f)) * 1000f)
math_steps.sub_desc: Solves closed-cycle gas pressure from harmonic cylinder volume changes.

math_steps.note: Pressure forces on hot and cold pistons generate driving shaft torque
math_steps.code:
// 2. Instantaneous gas pressure torque and flywheel angular acceleration
val pDiffKPa = pressureKPa - 101.3f
val torqueHot = pDiffKPa * sin(crankAngleRad) * forceScale
val torqueCold = pDiffKPa * sin(crankAngleRad - phaseOffsetRad) * forceScale
val netTorque = (torqueHot + torqueCold) - frictionTorque - effectiveLoad
angularVelocityRadS = max(0f, angularVelocityRadS + (netTorque / flywheelInertia) * dt)
math_steps.sub_desc: Integrates piston torque and rotational inertia to accelerate the flywheel.

math_steps.badge: EQUATION 3 OF 3 • NET WORK & CARNOT EFFICIENCY
math_steps.formula: W_net = ∮ P dV,  η_Stirling = W_net / Q_in ≤ 1 - T_C / T_H
math_steps.note: Regenerator thermal recovery approaches the theoretical Carnot ceiling
math_steps.code:
// 3. Indicated cycle work and thermal Carnot efficiency
val carnotEff = max(0f, 1f - (coldTempK / max(hotTempK, 1f)))
val thermalEff = carnotEff * regeneratorEff * 0.62f
val pMeanPa = pressureKPa * 1e3f
indicatedWorkJ = max(0.1f, pMeanPa * deltaVMaxMin * (hotTempK - coldTempK) / max(hotTempK, 1f) * 0.85f)
mechanicalPowerW = max(0f, (netTorque + effectiveLoad) * angularVelocityRadS * 0.75f)
math_steps.sub_desc: Computes closed-loop indicated work and thermal conversion efficiency.

en.title: Stirling Heat Engine
en.teaser: A sealed mass of gas shuttles cyclically between hot and cold reservoirs, converting pure heat into rotational work.

en.hook: How can an engine run silently on the warmth of your palm alone, producing mechanical power with zero exhaust?
en.math: By shuttling a sealed gas between hot and cold cylinders through a thermal regenerator, heat expands gas at high pressure and compresses it cold.
en.question: Can we simulate the Stirling cycle, Schmidt pressure equations, and flywheel dynamics live in Kotlin Multiplatform?
en.code_tip: We model closed-cycle Schmidt pressure equations, evaluate flywheel angular dynamics, and render real-time P-V indicator loops.
en.payoff: The Stirling heat engine running live in Kotlin.
